fuel: heptane and methanol droplets (n-heptane, alkane droplets)
objective: The objective of the FLEX is to study heptane and methanol droplets in ambient mixtures of oxygen and nitrogen diluted with a second inert gas (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon) to examine how the addition of an inert gas suppressant influences the flammability limit of the two fuels. It also provides benchmark data on radiative and diffusive extinction, combustion instabilities, and cool flames.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
conditionsMentioned: reduced gravity / microgravity; MDCA: 1 to 5 mm droplets in 0-3 atm ambient environment of up to 40 percent oxygen by volume; Figure 2: 70 percent carbon dioxide, 21 percent oxygen, balance nitrogen, translated at 3 cm/s

fuel: mixtures of pure fuels, real fuel surrogates, ethanol, liquid, biologically derived fuels
objective: Builds upon FLEX to study a range of fuels including mixtures of pure fuels, real fuel surrogates, soot formation, slow sub-buoyant convective flow effects, droplet-droplet interactions, flame propagation in droplet arrays, and liquid biologically derived fuels. It is motivated by the need to better understand droplet combustion for fundamental problems of energy conversion and utilization.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity; slow sub-buoyant convective flow; Figure 3: 30 percent oxygen at pressure of 2.4 atm

objective: Focused on soot processes, flame-vortex interaction, and flame stability in laminar, axisymmetric, gas-jet diffusion flames. Specifically, LSP studied soot processes in ambient configurations within sealed chambers.
hardware: Combustion Module (CM) facility, sealed chambers (STS-83, STS-94, and STS-107 space shuttle missions)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (space shuttle missions STS-83, STS-94, STS-107); ambient configuration

objective: Focused on soot processes, flame-vortex interaction, and flame stability using a laminar, axisymmetric, gas-jet diffusion flame where an iris mechanism around its base induced vortices in the entrained air.
hardware: Get-Away-Special Canister (GAS Can) in the payload bay, sealed chamber with iris mechanism (STS-87 space shuttle mission)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (space shuttle mission STS-87)

objective: Studied laminar, axisymmetric, gas-jet diffusion flames within a fan-driven flow duct, focusing on soot processes, flame-vortex interaction, and flame stability.
hardware: Middeck Glovebox, fan-driven flow duct (STS-87 space shuttle mission)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (space shuttle mission STS-87); fan-driven flow

objective: Studied soot processes in a coflow configuration within a fan-driven flow duct and investigated the transition from non-sooting to sooting with a major goal to provide simple predictions of soot emissions.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) on the ISS, fan-driven flow duct
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); coflow configuration, fan-driven flow

objective: Investigates the structure of lifting and lifted flames where flow conditions and combustion chemistry cause the flame to detach from the burner and stabilize at a downstream position. Its twin purposes are increased fuel efficiency and reduced pollutant emission by advancing combustion modeling capability.
hardware: SPICE hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); increasing coflow velocity

fuel: gaseous fuels (used to simulate paper, plastic, and alcohol)
objective: Improve fundamental understanding of materials flammability, such as ignition and extinction behavior, and assess the relevance of existing flammability test methods for low- and partial-gravity environments. Burning of solid and liquid fuels will be simulated using a flat porous burner fed with gaseous fuel controlled based on measured heat flux and surface temperature.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) modular hardware, flat porous burner (porous plate burner)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS), low- and partial-gravity environments

objective: Extend the range of flame conditions that can be accurately predicted by developing and experimentally verifying chemical kinetic and soot formation submodels. Measurements will be made of the structure of diluted methane and ethylene lifted flames in an air coflow at both very dilute and highly sooting conditions.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) modular hardware, gas-jet flame configuration with coaxial air flow
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); air coflow

fullName: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
objective: Gain an improved understanding of flame-ion production and investigate how ions can be used to control non-premixed flames. Measurements of ion current through the flame and the flame's response time to electric forcing will be made as a function of field strength and fuel dilution.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) modular hardware, burner with a flat, circular mesh suspended downstream
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); high-voltage electric field up to 10 kV differential

objective: Improve understanding of soot inception and control to enable optimization of oxygen-enriched combustion and the design of robust, soot-free non-premixed flames. It will investigate soot inception and extinction limits of spherical microgravity flames and explore whether the stoichiometric mixture fraction can characterize soot and flammability limits.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) modular hardware, porous spherical burner (or coflow burner if inverse spherical flame testing is not approved)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); oxygen-enriched atmosphere; Figure 6 drop tower test: 1.51 mg/s of 100 percent ethylene into air at atmospheric pressure

fullName: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
fuel: hydrogen, methane, and ethylene (Figure 7 drop tower test: propane)
objective: Advance the ability to predict the structure and dynamics, including radiative and convective extinction limits, of both soot-free and sooty spherical diffusion flames. Another objective is to determine the existence, onset, and nature of pulsating instabilities in fuel/diluent mixtures above a critical Lewis number.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) modular hardware, porous spherical burner
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); various inert diluents in fuel and chamber atmosphere; Figure 7 drop tower test: 25 percent propane, 2 percent oxygen, 49 percent argon, 24 percent nitrogen

fuel: flat samples (2cm acrylic flat sample), polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) spheres (2-cm diameter acrylic sphere), porous wax slabs, wax candles, 2-cm wide cotton-fiberglass fabric
objective: Examine the burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of solid fuel samples in microgravity to improve 1-g material fire safety rating tests and help guide strategies for extinguishing accidental fires in microgravity. It also guides combustion computational models used in designing fire detection and suppression systems.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE flow duct
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); nominally 21 percent oxygen by volume and 1 atmospheric pressure, nitrogen-diluted tests as low as 17 percent oxygen; Figure 2c: 17 percent oxygen and 10 cm/s flow; Figure 11: 17 percent oxygen and 12 cm/s flow; Figure 12: opposed flow decreased from 10 cm/s down to less than 1 cm/s

fullName: Correlation of Flammability between Normal and Microgravity
fuel: select materials / actual engineering materials planned for spacecraft
objective: Obtain the microgravity flammability map for select materials as a function of ventilation flow, ambient oxygen concentration, and possibly pressure to find the fundamental limiting oxygen concentration in microgravity. Comparison with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 normal gravity upward flame spread will enable evaluation of oxygen margins of safety.
hardware: SoFIE CIR insert and large flow duct within the MSG
conditionsMentioned: normal gravity and microgravity; SoFIE chamber: oxygen 10 percent to 40 percent by volume, pressure 0.2 to 1.5 atm, airflows 0 to 30 cm/s

fullName: Fundamentals of Flame Growth and Extinction in Microgravity
objective: Understand the fundamental processes of flame growth, spread, and decay over solid materials and their dependence on gravity, flow velocity, oxygen percentage, pressure, sample size, and preheating. Experimental results will be used to develop a numerical model to relate material flammability between normal and reduced gravity and examine NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.
hardware: SoFIE CIR insert and large flow duct within the MSG
conditionsMentioned: normal and reduced gravity / microgravity (ISS); SoFIE chamber: oxygen 10 percent to 40 percent by volume, pressure 0.2 to 1.5 atm, airflows 0 to 30 cm/s

fullName: Thermal and Species Field Effects on Material Flammability
objective: Determine flame spread rate over thin fuels in quiescent microgravity and measure gas phase temperature and concentration fields of carbon dioxide and oxygen to delineate propagation of the thermal field from the species field. This will establish quantitative criteria determining material flammability where radiative heat transfer dominates.
hardware: SoFIE CIR insert and large flow duct within the MSG
conditionsMentioned: quiescent microgravity and normal gravity; varying fuel thickness and ambient pressure; SoFIE chamber: oxygen 10 percent to 40 percent by volume, pressure 0.2 to 1.5 atm

fullName: External Heat Flux Effects on the Ignitability and Suppression of Materials in Microgravity
objective: Conduct microgravity ignition and suppression experiments for materials burning in low-speed, forced flow with externally applied heat flux in Space Exploration Atmospheres (SEA), measuring time to ignition and time between suppression agent introduction and extinction. Experiments will validate a comprehensive model of piloted ignition and extinction in SEA.
hardware: SoFIE CIR insert and large flow duct within the MSG
conditionsMentioned: microgravity, normal-gravity buoyant flows, low-speed forced flow, Space Exploration Atmospheres (SEA); SoFIE chamber: oxygen 10 percent to 40 percent by volume, pressure 0.2 to 1.5 atm, airflows 0 to 30 cm/s

fullName: Narrow Channel as a 1-g Flammability Test Method
objective: Measure flame spread rate and opposed flow extinction limits across a representative, thick, solid fuel as a function of forced opposed flow velocity, oxygen concentration, and pressure corresponding to NASA's SEA in microgravity. Data will determine if an optimum gap height in the 1-g Narrow Channel device can reproduce microgravity results.
hardware: Narrow Channel device (1-g), SoFIE CIR insert and large flow duct within the MSG
conditionsMentioned: 1-g (normal gravity) and microgravity; NASA's Space Exploration Atmospheres (SEA); SoFIE chamber: oxygen 10 percent to 40 percent by volume, pressure 0.2 to 1.5 atm, airflows 0 to 30 cm/s

fullName: Structure of Flame Balls at Low Lewis-number
objective: Studied stationary, spherical premixed flames (flame balls) in very fuel-lean, low Lewis-number gas mixtures in microgravity. It validated prior theoretical predictions, improved understanding of combustion reactions near extinction limits, and provided pure test beds for numerical modeling.
hardware: Combustion Module (CM) facility, large combustion chamber (STS-83, STS-94, and STS-107 space shuttle missions)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (STS-83, STS-94, STS-107); very fuel-lean conditions, low Lewis number

fuel: various fuel and oxygen mixtures (premixed flame)
objective: Measure the extinguishing capability of water mist on a premixed flame propagating along a tube and study how water droplet diameter and water concentration affect the speed, strength, and shape of flames. The results helped design more effective mist fire-suppression systems to replace banned Halon systems.
hardware: Combustion Module (CM) facility (space shuttle mission STS-107)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (space shuttle mission STS-107 in 2003)

objective: Examined the background aerosol particulate levels on the ISS to address issues related to spacecraft fire detection.
hardware: International Space Station (ISS)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS)

objective: Examined the particle-size distribution of the smoke from spacecraft materials in microgravity to provide useful guidance for the designers of future spacecraft smoke detectors.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) on the ISS
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS)

fuel: methanol in water (methanol 10 weight percent) with air oxidizer (ZGF tests); cellulosic material (1990s Ames ground tests)
objective: Assess the impact of buoyancy on Super-Critical Water Oxidation (SCWO) processes and determine the extent to which buoyancy affects the developing temperature profile. A second objective to measure reaction rate and product concentrations with Raman spectroscopy was not met due to budgetary constraints.
hardware: SCWO Test Facility with 500-ml reactor vessel in the Zero Gravity Facility (ZGF, 5.2-second drop tower)
conditionsMentioned: 0-g / microgravity (5.2-second drop tower) and 1-g / normal gravity; super-critical water mixture; methanol 10 weight percent

fuel: water-salt mixture using Na2SO4 (0.5 percent w/v); pure water (July 2010 baseline test)
objective: Investigate the behavior of salt precipitate formation and transport in super-critical water in the presence of temperature gradients. This will provide practical insights into the mechanisms of salt agglomeration, transport, and deposition that often plague SCWO reactors.
hardware: Refurbished High Temperature Insert (HTI-R) built by CNES on the ISS (baseline test conducted in HTI)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); raised to temperature and pressure above critical point; approximately 0.3 cm3 fluid cell filled with Na2SO4 (0.5 percent w/v) at critical density

objective: Investigated the behavior of a simple candle flame in a long-duration microgravity environment aboard the Russian Mir orbiting station to test whether a steady flame can exist without buoyancy and observe near-extinction flame oscillations.
hardware: Russian Mir orbiting station
conditionsMentioned: 0-g / long-duration microgravity (Mir) and normal gravity comparison

fullName: SCWO research facility for the ISS
objective: Investigate the effects of buoyancy in SCWO reactors and enable progression of SCWO technology for NASA life support to higher technology readiness levels (TRLs). Science objectives include studying hydrodynamics of sub-critical and super-critical mixing, reaction zone characterization, heat transfer in super-critical fluids, and precipitate transport.
hardware: Express Rack on the ISS, ~1-liter reactor with removable base, two cameras, collimated backlight, Raman spectrometer, and temperature, pressure, and flow sensors
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); sub-critical and super-critical conditions

objective: Proposed alternative insert for the DECLIC facility to accomplish a limited subset of the ISS SCWO science scope, restricted to quasi-steady processes without Raman spectroscopic chemical kinetic studies.
hardware: DEvice for the study of Critical LIquids and Crystallization (DECLIC) facility insert (reactor volume ~0.5 percent of Option 1, single optical axis)
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); super-critical conditions

objective: Use a range of fuel types and environmental conditions to determine necessary pre-conditions for hot-flame/cool-flame transitions, cool flame stability, and spontaneous re-ignition, and develop a robust numerical modeling capability with detailed chemistry to complement analytical Cool Flame Theory.
hardware: Existing FLEX-2 CIR/MDCA hardware augmented with additional diagnostic capabilities
conditionsMentioned: reduced-gravity / microgravity (ISS); range of pressure and diluent concentrations

objective: Series of investigations directed toward carbon sequestration and pollution reduction.
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS)

objective: New initiative envisioned for future ISS research investigating self-assembling propellants and catalysts.
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS)

objective: New initiative envisioned for future ISS research focusing on high pressures as related to (i) engines and (ii) supernova formation.
conditionsMentioned: microgravity (ISS); high pressures

objective: New initiative focusing on developing a Fire Database Reference containing information on such things as transport measurements at flame conditions, flame speeds, and chemical kinetics.
